propositions: The AC1 snapshot-equivalence contract in test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py does not actually drive the real MCP and reconciler entry points; instead it re-calls the shared composer with identical arguments, which trivially passes even if those surfaces stop routing through the composer.
The MCP surface block must invoke the real entry point via build_server() and call_tool() instead of re-calling compose_operation_snapshot().
The reconciler surface block must invoke the real argv entry point rebar_reconciler.__main__.main() with --dry-run-enumerate instead of re-calling compose_operation_snapshot().
Each surface block must fail with an explicit assertion when its surface composes no operation snapshot, to catch routing breakage rather than silently passing over an empty capture.

Each surface block must anchor its assertions to absolute expected content (repo root, envelope version, config keys with distinct provenance) in addition to comparing results to the Python reference, because cross-surface equality alone is vacuous under composer perturbation.
